title: dialogue block props
description: A branching conversation held in one block (D61): its nodes (a few lines, then a way out: options the learner chooses, a jump, an end), its endings and its score. The learner plays a speaker (learner) whose options become their bubbles; characters answer with lines. The thread grows in the block; the player keeps the path, replays it on resume, scores the first run and records one SCORM interaction per decision.
x-ai-instructions: Write the best path first, then the other options. Short lines (one or two sentences). Each decision: about three options, good, ok and bad (quality), plausible and of similar length, never with a speaker. Show the consequence first (reply, a character's reaction), the trainer's note after (feedback), never in a character's mouth. An option without next joins the node's way out: branch only where the story really differs, and join back. Check with elabora dialogue paths and elabora dialogue play (skill elabora-dialogues).

title.description: The dialogue's accessible name, read by screen readers and shown on its start card and debrief (« L'appel de Marc »).

learner.description: The speaker of course.json speakers the learner plays: their options become this speaker's bubbles. Absent: the bubbles say « Vous » (a player label).

learnerVoice.description: The learner's options are said by the voice of learner, as lines (with learner).

style.description: messaging: a chat thread, characters on the left with a round portrait, the learner on the right (slides and scroll pages). scene: a backdrop and the cast drawn large, a few bubbles near them, the full thread in a History (slides; scroll pages too).

scene.description: Style scene: the backdrop and the cast placed on it. A node may change the backdrop (its scene).

mode.description: Sets revisit, feedback and scoring at once (each stays changeable). practice: retry during the run, then back to any choice after the first end; feedback now and in the debrief; not scored. assessment: no going back, feedback in the debrief only, scored by quality. exploration: back to any choice at any time, feedback now, not scored.

revisit.description: How the learner may go back (default: the mode's). none: never (retry options continue instead). retry: « Choisir autrement » right after a consequence, and options with retry come back. after-end: retry, then « Reprendre d'ici » on any past choice and « Recommencer » once the first end is reached. anytime: « Reprendre d'ici » from the first choice. The first run to an end is the only one scored, whatever the policy; a final decision cannot be revisited, nor anything before it, but once the dialogue has ended « Recommencer » still starts a new run.

scoring.description: What the dialogue's score (0 to 1, like any activity) is made of (default: the mode's). quality: good 1, ok 0.5, bad 0, the mean over the decisions met. points: the sum of the options' points over the highest sum a path can reach (computed on the graph). ending: the score of the ending reached. none: not scored. Scored dialogues count in the course score with weight, and record one choice interaction per decision of the first run.

weight.description: Weight in the course score, when scored.

objective.description: The plan objective the dialogue practises: the objective of its SCORM interactions. A node or an option may name its own.

feedback.description: When the options' feedback is shown (default: the mode's): now, as a trainer's note in the thread after the consequence; debrief, in the debrief card at the end; both.

debrief.description: A debrief card at the end: the ending reached, each decision with its quality and feedback, then the other endings.

pace.description: auto: the voiced lines of a turn follow one another; a text without a voice (a line without audio, a note) waits for the learner's « Suite ». click: one line per click.

reveal.description: How a line's words come in step with its voice: ink (words not said yet in a faint ink), appear (they appear), instant (the whole text at once). A line without a voice, reduced motion and the learner's « Texte : tout de suite » show the whole text.

begins.description: auto: when the block comes into view (or its step is revealed). click: a start card with a button. event: when an event runs start-dialogue.

start.description: The first node (default: the first of nodes).

vars.description: Variables of the dialogue only (a character's trust…), changed by options (set, add) and read by conditions ({ "var": "trust", "op": "gte", "value": 2 }). Recomputed from the path, so they go back when the learner goes back. Never the course's variables: those change on dialogue.ended, in an event of the screen.

default.description: The value at the start; its type is the variable's.

nodes.description: The moments of the conversation, in reading order. A node plays its lines, then leaves by, in this order: its options (a decision), its next, its end, or else the next node of the list (after the last one, the dialogue ends).

endings.description: Named endings. end: true lets their conditions choose (the first that holds wins; put one without if last); end: "<id>" picks one. Without endings, the dialogue ends without a title.

dialogueNodeId.description: Identifier of a node, unique in its dialogue: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Permanent once learners played: their saved path names options by node.

background.description: The backdrop: an image or an SVG of assets/ (decorative).

cast.description: Who is on stage and where.

dialogueLine.description: A line, as a narration line is (id, speaker, text, delivery, pronunciations), with what the drawing does (expression, cues) and a condition (if). Without speaker, a narration: a setting of the scene shown without a character's bubble (« Plus tard, au bureau de Marc »); a speaker declared narrator in course.json says it with its voice, still without a bubble.

id.description: Unique in the screen, across the screen's narration, its layers and its dialogues: the line's audio, translation and anchors are named by it.

speaker.description: A speaker of course.json speakers. Absent: a narration without voice.

text.description: What is said, word for word: the bubble, the voice and its captions. Words in square brackets are stage directions for an expressive voice ([inquiet], [soupire]): never shown nor counted as words. Keep it short: one or two sentences.

delivery.description: How a generated voice says this line, by language: settings over those of the speaker's voice in that language, for example { "fr": { "speed": 1.1 } }.

pronunciations.description: How a generated voice says words of this line, by language, before those of the course.

expression.description: The face the speaker shows from this line on, until another line or cue changes it: one of the expressions their look declares. Distinct from a stage direction, which tells the voice how to say it.

cues.description: Moments on the words of this line: a gesture, an expression, or presentation actions on the screen (show a photo when Marc says « imprimante »).

if.description: The line is skipped unless every condition holds.

at.description: A moment of this line, as a timeline anchor (D28) without its line: a word or a few words ({ "word": "Bonjour" }), their end (edge end), an offset in seconds; {} or { "edge": "end" } for the line itself.

line.description: Implicit: the cue's own line. When written, it must be that line.

word.description: One or a few words of the line, as written there.

gesture.description: A gesture the speaker's look declares (data-gestures of its SVG), played at that moment.

expression.description: The speaker's face from that moment on.

do.description: Presentation actions on the screen at that moment.

dialogueAction.description: What a dialogue may do to its screen: show-block, hide-block, show-layer, hide-layer, play-media, pause-media, set-object-props, reveal-step (presentation only: replaying a path sets the last visibility and props of the blocks it touched, and opens no layer). A dialogue never writes the course's variables nor navigates: do that on dialogue.ended, in an event of the screen.

props.description: set-object-props: values for declared props only.

dialogueConditions.description: All must hold (AND). For OR, write two options, or next cases where the first that holds wins.

dialogueCondition.description: { "chosen": "node.option" }: the option was chosen on the current path. { "seen": "node" }: the node is on the current path. { "var": "trust", "op": "gte", "value": 2 }: a variable of the dialogue. { "score": { "op": "gte", "value": 80 } }: the current score out of 100 (the quality score when the dialogue is not scored). { "variable": "role", "op": "eq", "value": "tech" }: a variable of the course, read only.

dialogueEnd.description: true: the endings' conditions choose (the first that holds). An ending's id: that ending.

title.description: For authors only (the script, the map): « Conséquence A ». Never shown to learners.

objective.description: The plan objective this decision practises (default: the dialogue's).

final.description: A final decision (« Choix définitif », announced before the choice): no going back to it, nor before it.

scene.description: Style scene: the backdrop (and cast) from this node on.

lines.description: Said in order when the node is entered; a line whose if fails is skipped.

prompt.description: The instruction over the options (« Quelle question posez-vous en premier ? »).

options.description: A decision: what the learner may say. One option shown is not taken by itself: the learner clicks it.

next.description: Where the node goes after its lines (or where its options go when they have no next of their own): a node id, or cases where the first whose if holds wins ([{ "if": [ … ], "go": "a" }, { "go": "b" }]: end with a case without if).

dialogueOption.description: What the learner may say (always the learner: an option has no speaker). Without next, it joins the node's way out (its next, its end, else the next node): a decision with a reaction and a note per option, then one common thread, needs no wiring.

id.description: Unique in its node, permanent (learners' saved paths name it).

text.description: What the learner says: their bubble (and a voice line with learnerVoice).

label.description: The button's words, when shorter than text.

quality.description: Good, ok or bad: never shown before the choice; the score (quality), the debrief and SCORM (correct, neutral, wrong) read it.

objective.description: The plan objective this choice puts into play.

reply.description: The immediate reaction: lines said after the learner's bubble.

feedback.description: The trainer's note on this choice, shown as a note (never a character's bubble) after the reaction, when the dialogue's feedback says now or both, and in the debrief.

points.description: What the choice is worth (scoring points).

add.description: Adds to number variables of the dialogue: { "trust": -1 }.

do.description: Presentation actions on the screen when the option is chosen.

next.description: A jump to a node (default: the node's way out).

retry.description: After the reaction and the feedback, the same options come back, this one greyed (the first choice still counts).

once.description: Gone (or greyed, with unavailable disable) once taken on the path: a hub of questions.

fallback.description: Never shown; taken by itself when no other option can be chosen.

if.description: Offered only when every condition holds.

unavailable.description: What an option whose if fails (or a once option taken) does: hidden, or shown greyed.

unavailableText.description: With disable: why it cannot be chosen yet.

title.description: Shown at the top of the debrief (« Maîtrisé »).

text.description: What this ending means for the learner.

if.description: With end: true, the first ending whose conditions hold is reached.

score.description: scoring ending: the score this ending gives, out of 100.
